reason: Feasibility lens: the refined idea survives. It builds nothing new: a finals decision rule based on probes 29/30, plus one optional replay readout. Everything it needs already exists. (1) Kernel: EDGEFILTER_CAPTURE (tools/build_probe_kernel.py l.617) is inserted at _EF_RELINK_ANCHOR, before the motion relink and before linefit. The ILP edges and PRE-linefit node coordinates are both in scope there, so a per-t median ILP step and a frozen flag take about 10 more lines, at negligible runtime. The edgefilter call runs after linefit (l.631), and an 'only flagged t' restriction is one extra candidate test in edgefilter_final_graph, a no-op by default. (2) Replay: run_config_video -> load_ilp_probs (replay.py l.836) already reads raw/<stem>.geff with the raw pre-linefit detector coordinates, applying the kernel's own next-frame/length filter. The per-t flag takes about 15 lines there, and an ef.anom_min_step_um knob about 20-30 lines in the shared patch text. The lab has fixed nodes and edge probabilities, and ef is a pure post-linefit graph edit, so the replay is exact for this. (3) No conflict with the pipeline: the kernel order linefit -> edgefilter -> swapfix -> stitch -> divinsert is unchanged; the restriction only shrinks ef's candidate set. Leaf prune (before linefit) and DaughterNet insertion (after) are untouched. Stitch reads the same ilp_probs, unaffected. (4) Cost: 2 configs x 135 confirmation videos on the Kaggle CPU lab, the same job shape as ef-a3-conf (4 workers), well within a day. Real pitfalls, all repairable, none fatal: (a) The research flag used the median of relink_ilp_tight edges from the parquet. The kernel and replay can only cheaply use the median of ALL captured ILP edges, so the 3.5 um threshold must be re-read in the replay itself, not carried over from the parquet. (b) Changing the edgefilter patch text changes _edgefilter_sha, so ef config fingerprints change: re-run the plain ef reference in the same lab job. (c) The exact-zero frozen test (len_pre==0 on >80% of edges) will break once the x138 coordinate head ships. Coordinates become float, and the TemporalUNet's context differs for t and t+1 even when the volumes are identical, so steps become small but nonzero. Use a tolerance (e.g. median ILP step < 0.2 um) or raw-volume equality. (d) ef was validated only on the integer-coordinate cache, and the replay CANNOT test ef on top of coordhead (fixed detector nodes). Any final that combines coordhead+ef must therefore be checked by one LB probe (exp51+ef). 5 slots/day with 5 days left makes that affordable, but the finals policy must name this probe explicitly. (e) The 4 dummy test clips are train copies, so the kernel log only verifies the code path. The original ef_anom with the relative 1.8x flag is also implementable, but the research shows it discards 25-55% of ef's gain, so feasibility is not its problem. The refined 'do not build ef_anom' is the right call.
fix_if_any: Keep the refined plan: no ef_anom build or probe; the finals policy is keyed on S29/S30. If the optional readout is run: compute the per-t flag from load_ilp_probs' raw pre-linefit coordinates (replay) and inside EDGEFILTER_CAPTURE (kernel), using the median of all captured ILP edge lengths per t. Re-calibrate the step threshold on the replay's own class readout. Detect frozen transitions with a tolerance (median ILP step < ~0.2 um), not exact zero, so the rule survives coordhead's float coordinates. Re-run the plain ef reference in the same lab job because the patch hash changes. For finals: since the replay cannot evaluate ef on coordhead nodes, spend one LB slot on exp51 + ef_a3_rl_pr (+stitch) before ticking a coordhead+ef final. Under policy (b) the two finals then become (coordhead best without ef) and (coordhead + ef).
realistic_public_gain: Direct public gain of the refined change: 0 (the public effect of ef is read from probe 29, and ef_anom ~= ef within 0.0006 locally). Value is in the private hedge: keeping ef in one final after a flat public result may be worth ~+0.002..+0.008 private, depending on how often the hidden embryos have frozen or fast transitions. Implementation cost is under half a day plus one Kaggle CPU lab run; the only extra LB slot is the coordhead+ef compatibility probe.
